title: Universal structured log ingress and enrichment bridge
creator: Arjun Mehta
description:
Short: Build a unified structured log ingress bridge that normalizes heterogeneous sources, attaches canonical correlation IDs, enriches with tenant/context metadata, and fans out to multiple downstream sinks (Loki, Elasticsearch, BigQuery) with backpressure and idempotency. This replaces ad-hoc shims and reduces per-tenant parsing duplication.

Goals:
- Accept JSON and semi-structured logs from edge agents and services.
- Apply dynamic parsing adapters and schema registry lookups.
- Canonicalize trace and correlation IDs (allow mapping of X-Request-Id, TRACE_ID, ctx.request_id).
- Emit a single canonical envelope with metadata for downstream consumers.
- Support multitenant routing and per-tenant retention/sampling policies.
- Provide observability and health metrics, and support gradual rollout with feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress accepts JSON and common log formats with <2ms processing median per event in warm path
Canonical correlation_id field present for 100% of events via mapping or generation
Enrichment step attaches tenant_id and service mapping with >=99.9% accuracy for known hosts
Fanout to Loki/ES/BigQuery succeeds with per-sink retry/backoff and idempotency keys
End-to-end latency SLO: 95th percentile < 500ms to sink for non-batched paths
Smoke dashboards created in Grafana and shared with SRE and Observability PMs
updates: 2025-02-12: Created ticket. Initial discovery notes and strawman architecture in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Universal+Log+Ingress+Bridge
2025-02-17: Spike completed for parser adapters. Implemented prototype adapter for syslog->JSON and cloudwatch-like records. Results documented: average parse time 0.9ms per record at 10k RPS.
2025-02-21: Chose Kubernetes-based ingress service (Knative-like) for autoscaling with a sidecar for tenant identification. Decision: prefer streaming gRPC from edge for reduced head latency.
2025-02-28: Design review with PM and Security. Feedback: must add canonical id mapping table and KMS integration for tenant metadata. Security asked for retention metadata in envelope.
2025-03-03: Implemented enrichment pipeline with KV cache for recent host->service mappings. WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/log-bridge/pull/142
2025-03-05: Load test results: 50k RPS sustained with 3ms median processing (in-memory cache warm). Observability metrics emitted to staging Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/ingest-health
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High QPS from bursty tenants can cause downstream sink throttling. Mitigation: implement per-tenant queueing and adaptive sampling, plus per-tenant rate limits and backpressure propagation.
Risk: Schema drift causing downstream consumers to break. Mitigation: integrate schema registry and schema version in envelope; emit validation metrics and rejection counters.
Risk: Incorrect correlation ID mapping leading to fragmented traces. Mitigation: fallback generation policy and lookup table with TTL; include original headers for traceability.
migration_plan: Phase 0: Canary ingest in staging for internal services only. Mirror small subset of prod traffic to staging bridge for validation.
Phase 1: Side-by-side run: run bridge in front of current shims with mirroring to new sinks for 7 days. Validate counts and latency metrics.
Phase 2: Gradual tenant cutover by feature flag in 10% increments every 48 hours with automated rollbacks on error budget burn.
Phase 3: Deprecate legacy shims and remove duplicated transformations after 30 days of stable run.
test_plan: Unit tests for parser adapters and canonicalization rules with >90% coverage
Integration tests with Loki and Elasticsearch test clusters using real-ish events
Chaos test: inject downstream 429s and validate backpressure and retry behavior
Load test at 2x expected peak to validate autoscaling and queueing
